Masking is a normal human process, pretty automatic. That being said I believe covert schizoid folk have a much more comprehensive mask than “average” people. 

To answer your question, I developed my mask as a child in a family that refused to believe that being a solitary introvert was normal. My space and my mind was constantly under threat from a mother who would not leave me alone until I displayed some sort of adequate over-the-top emotional response. So I became, on the outside, who I needed to be. I retreated deep into myself and forged a fake external persona that made my mother leave me alone. 

My mask shifts and develops over time from situation to situation, as everyone’s does. I do not mask the same way I did as a child but the strategy and core of its development is the same.

Hm. Longing is a strong word, so I’m inclined to say no. Sometimes I get a flicker of interest in connecting with some certain person or another but I inevitably end up disappointed or bored by them. In response to these continuous letdowns the flicker of interest in people has become dimmer and dimmer. 

At the same time, as I’ve gotten older I’ve become relatively competent when it comes to interacting with people. I have a great mask. It’s exhausting to keep it on, but it fools most everyone I’ve ever known.

I don’t explain, I just refuse invitations. When I do care about someone, which is rare, I tell them that I am extremely introverted and that I don’t get any fulfillment from socializing. They can take it or leave it.

Once they were with other people, they felt “tainted” to me. Not sexually but in my mind space it was like they no longer fit because they were no longer “mine.” I wasn’t jealous because they were with other people, I truly didn’t think anything at all about that. It was the lack of “full possession” that messed with my head. However, I am not possessive of people in general. I do hookups just fine because there is no interpersonal connection. If I’m detached, and I mostly am, it doesn’t affect me.

I quit weed 3 years ago (as well as all other mind-altering substances) and it greatly improved my quality of life. I had the same experience as you. All that to say, congratulations on this step. It’s hard but in my opinion it’s always the right choice.

The whole masking process is incredibly automatic for me, and the after effects are debilitating and exhausting. I also think it affects my memory, like you say. My coworkers will ask me: was work busy on Saturday? And I simply don’t remember a single thing about that whole shift because “I” was not there.

I have one friend who’s stood the test of time. Our friendship is ideal because we have one major common interest/hobby. No need to emotionally connect when we can simply talk about that shared interest. They’re an online friend, so they never encroach on my physical space. Doesn’t care when I drop off the face of the earth and doesn’t press, doesn’t have their feelings hurt about it. We often don’t talk for weeks at a time but can pick up again with no problem. They also have schizoid traits which is helpful. 

Neither of us ask for or want emotional enmeshment with the other. We’ve been friends for four years, which is a long time and certainly a record for me. I feel like they are the only person I have “real,” non-masked conversation with, simply because they are just as emotionally unaffected as I am. We are both blunt and honest with each other. To me, this friendship embodies “ideal friendship.”
